subject: marketing
intro: Marketing leads to the commercial functions that match products to customers — managing brands, researching markets, running sales organisations and shaping how firms are seen.

roles.title: Marketing Managers
roles.what: Plan and direct marketing policies and programmes: estimate demand for products and services, identify potential customers, set pricing strategies and oversee product development and market trends.
roles.where: The segmentation, targeting and positioning unit is the manager's working framework, the pricing topic of the price and promotion unit is theirs to set, and the competitive analysis unit is the standing briefing they commission.

roles.title: Market Research Analysts and Marketing Specialists
roles.what: Research conditions in local, regional, national or online markets, gathering data on competitors, prices and sales to plan campaigns and analyse web metrics for better search performance.
roles.where: The customer analysis units — value to the customer and customer lifetime value — are the calculations analysts run, and the market-strategy unit's need for evidence is exactly what market research supplies.

roles.title: Sales Managers
roles.what: Plan and coordinate how a product or service reaches the customer: set sales territories, quotas and goals, train sales representatives and analyse sales statistics and customer preferences.
roles.where: The price, promotion and distribution unit covers the channels a sales manager runs, and the customer analysis units are how territories and quotas get matched to the customers actually out there.

roles.title: Public Relations Specialists
roles.what: Promote or create an intended public image for individuals, groups or organisations, writing and selecting material for release across the media, increasingly through social platforms.
roles.where: The branding unit — what a brand promises and how it is perceived — is the raw material of public relations, and the international branding topic extends the same craft to firms entering foreign markets.

roles.title: Graphic Designers
roles.what: Design graphics to meet commercial or promotional needs — packaging, displays, logos and campaign artwork — working across print and digital mediums for brands and clients.
roles.where: The branding unit treats a logo and a product's look as strategy, not decoration, and the product and promotion units are where packaging and advertising design decisions get made with designers in the room.
